open_questions: Why stellar density penalty is elevated despite plausible duration — likely due to fitted high impact and spot-crossing not binary; Gaia RV not available to rule out low-mass companion by mass.

What drives 1.4% spot variability amplitude 13543 ppm in sector 46 vs different period 0.351 d in sector 91; multi-epoch RV and high-resolution photometry would confirm planet vs stellar variation in more sectors.
dossier.public_summary: A 1.2% flat-bottomed dip repeats every 12.6 days with a size of 4.3 Earth radii around a small M dwarf, duration matching the star. Depth is steady when the same pipeline is used, there is no secondary eclipse or odd-even difference, and no neighbour within a pixel can produce it, despite strong starspots. The star's own variation is much shorter, so a planet is the best explanation pending mass measurement.

reasons.why: Planet-sized around a small M dwarf, well below 10 Rearth, so eclipse would be other star if stellar.

0 plausible neighbours within 1 TESS pixel and closest that could need eclipses 0.4174 at 43.7 arcsec, so off-target/blend as cause is unlikely; inconclusive difference image does not indicate off-target.
Flat-bottomed transit shape, not V-shaped, favours planet over grazing binary; fit_b 0.7961 is high but not grazing given flat bottom.
Below 5 sigma threshold and not above best_brightening_snr 2.894, so no significant secondary eclipse; secondary well below dip depth.
No odd/even depth difference; depth_odd 14110 ppm vs depth_even 10920 ppm difference only 1.386 sigma so no binary at twice 25.2 d period.
Apparent 37% depth change (9605 ppm vs 14009 ppm, p_constant 0.02847) is between sources SPOC vs QLP; p_constant 1.0 within each source, so no true sector-depth variability.

Large spotted variability exists (FAP 4.6116725763922364e-09) as expected for Teff 3446 K M dwarf with phot_variable_flag NOT_AVAILABLE; variation exists but period 9.019 d is not an exact integer multiple of signal 12.6 d and phase-curve amplitude 863 ppm ratio 0.07191 chi2 7.267 dof 9 shows no significant out-of-dip modulation, so spots do not explain the flat 12.6 d dip.

Observed 2.499 h vs central 2.159 h fits M dwarf size; Gaia radii 0.387 FLAME / 0.399 GSP-Phot give ratios 1.07 / 1.04 and R 4.63 / 4.77 Rearth, still planet-sized; density penalty 16.61 flagged but likely due to rotation and eccentricity not stellar radius mismatch.
